eyebrow: Real SQL, against a Spark DataFrame
code:
df.createOrReplaceTempView("trips")

result = spark.sql("""
  SELECT VendorID, COUNT(*) AS trip_count, AVG(fare_amount) AS avg_fare
  FROM trips
  WHERE fare_amount > 0
  GROUP BY VendorID
""")
caption: If you've taken this site's T-SQL course, this syntax should look almost entirely familiar.

eyebrow: SQL API and DataFrame API — the SAME thing underneath
code:
-- IDENTICAL results, identical execution plan:
spark.sql("SELECT VendorID, COUNT(*) FROM trips WHERE fare_amount > 0 GROUP BY VendorID")

df.filter(df["fare_amount"] > 0).groupBy("VendorID").count()
caption: Spark's Catalyst optimizer doesn't care which syntax you started from — use whichever is more readable.

code:
result = spark.sql("SELECT * FROM trips WHERE fare_amount < 0")
# Nothing has run yet -- SAME lazy evaluation as Lesson 34.

result.show()   # THIS triggers it
caption: spark.sql() returns a DataFrame describing a plan — Lesson 35's action rule still applies.
